Let’s Look At Desert Ship (by FlavourArt)

Desert Ship is a reknown “base” tobacco flavoring by FlavourArt (out of Italy). Descriptions around the internet describe it as a ‘Turkish-spiced’ flavor with an ‘earthy tobacco’ profile that toes the line on ‘nutty.’ Scores of people love it, just as many hate it and don't ever want to touch it again. Some have no idea what to do with it!

This is one man’s opinion on the flavor profile, please feel free to debate any and all of these talking points in the comments!

So let’s get mixing, and see what works with it and what doesn’t.

There certainly is a bit of a base flavor that sits halfway between savory and sweet. Definitive, and distinguishable without obvious tells (like vanilla, or licorice) With it, I believe something of a nut variety was added as well, perhaps a really light Almond or Pecan to accent it.

Straight:

At 1% in 50/50 PG/VG - Super, super light. Light enough that it almost becomes a bit of an oak, woodsy kind of taste. Not too much in the sweetness, more of an accent that tastes a bit leathery, a bit dusty even. At this ratio, DS should prove to be a good addition to more complex tobacco mixes.

At 3% (50/50) - The overall tones of the flavor start to appear and make themselves be known. The sweetness appears and the nuttiness aspect becomes much more apparent. It’s full-bodied, resting peacefully in the middle of the flavor profile - probably why I, and many others, opt for it as a tobacco base rather than as an accent. The woodiness of it at one percent isn’t gone, but is more defined and doesn’t taste very ‘wood-y’ anymore. More of a musk at this point.

At 5% (50/50) - We’re right about at the sweet spot, in my opinion, for this flavor to be used as a start, or base, for a complex blend. The aforementioned muskiness is in full swing and dominates the profile, while the nuttiness becomes more apparent. It’s also noticeably sweeter than before. Depending on the amount of other flavors I want to cram into a bottle to make a recipe, this point is either going to make or break it. It might be better to tone it down if there’s a ton of other stuff going into it, otherwise you’ll be fighting the tone of it. At this point, I’m inclined to believe that DS will win, too.

Also, at 5%, I believe this is the sweet spot for a single-flavor mix. Standing by itself, five percent is perfect.

At 7% it’s simply a little too strong to be a stand-alone, and anything you throw at it (combo-wise) is going to be overshadowed and pushed back. In this, I’ll say that DS can start to get rather “aggressive.” At this level, you’d need to add a lot of other stuff for that other stuff to shine through. If you’re trying to do this, we’d probably get much better results by simply lowering the DS to a more manageable level. No one wants to vape 50% flavoring in their juice, do they?

Good mixers:

In my days of mixing, I’ve thrown a lot of different stuff at DS to see what stuck. Let’s take a look at some of the stuff that works decently well with it.

Tobaccos! The tobacco end of the spectrum shines brightly with DS, and there are a ton of them that combine perfectly. High-note, spicy tobaccos like FA Perique, FA Burley and FA Shade combine well at low percentages (say, 3% DS - 2% Burley, for example). FA Oakwood is a fantastic addition to a DS blend, emphasizing the woodsy, musky notes. TFA Cowboy and TFA M-Type blend decently with it as well, but remember to ratio your flavorings appropriately! M-Type only needs a very small nudge to change the profile altogether, but the effects are pleasant.

Coconut and DS is a match made in heaven, almost. Stronger coconuts will lend themselves to the middle ground that DS already stands in. They’ll make for a good, smooth combination (especially FA Coconut) and seem to blend super well. Candy-spectrum Coconut (like TFA Coconut Extra) conflict with it a bit however, paying extra attention to the natural sweetness of DS and turning it into a bit of a musky candy. Which struck me as kind of weird. Not bad, just... weird.

Nuts, like CAP Toasted Almond or LA Pecan blend well, thanks in no small part to the natural nuttiness hinted at in DS. It’s completely possible to use DS as a base to a nut mix. LA Black Walnut is one of my favorite nut flavors, and pairs well with it at low volumes.

Creams and custards are DS’s bedtime buddies as well, but with these flavors we might look at lowering DS to more of an accent flavor than a base. CAP Vanilla Custard V2 mixed at a low percentage with an even lower percentage of DS is a delight, and the custard notes play well with the middle ground DS stands firmly on. FA Vanilla Bourbon and FA Vienna Cream are easy to blend as well.

Fruits. I’ll put this at the end of the ‘Good’ column because it largely depends on what fruit you’re trying to use with it. Tropical flavors like pineapple, mango and banana can work well with it, bringing a bit of a fruity punch to a low-ratio base. Others, however, like most all sorts of apple, pomegranate, blue and blackberries, strawberry, honeydew melon and raspberry simply do not combine very well.

Bad Mixers:

Those are some of the things that I feel work really well with Desert Ship. Let’s look at some that don’t work too well.

Most non-tropical fruits. As mentioned above, these won’t work very well with DS - unless you’re hiding that fruit in a whole mess of other stuff that actually blend well, using DS as a complementary note instead of as a base.

Citrus. I’ve yet to be able to mix together citruses with it. FA Lemon Sicily and TFA Lemon-Lime lend a really odd hand to DS that make it taste... off. I don’t recommend those. Orange is a little bit different, especially Orange Cream flavors - those you can work with, in really low concentrations. But even then, you’ll likely be wanting to put additional fruits and custards in there to smooth everything out. Orange and DS straight is one funky monkey.

Mints. Some people are going to like a menthol vape no matter what’s mixed in with it, but I’m sad to say that I haven’t successfully gotten DS to blend with mint very well. Forget Koolada, the sensation along with the taste makes it quite perfume-heavy on the exhale, bizarre combination indeed. Spearmint, wintergreen, peppermint - none of these pair very well with DS. Mixing it with MBV’s Extreme Ice flavoring is a “go” preceded by a “no.”

Finally, another spectrum that doesn’t blend too well are the oddballs of FA’s catalog - things like FA Summer Wind and FA Zen Garden taste funky when combined with DS. These flavors tend to hint at more floral, perfume heavy taste profiles that conflict immediately with the middle-ground, musk and earthiness that DS brings to the table.

TL;DR -

Desert Ship is a good addition at 1-3%, a good base flavor at 3-5%, and isn’t very good past 5% alone.

Tobaccos, tobacco additives and ‘woodsy’ flavors are awesome with it. So are tropical fruits, creams, custards and bakery style flavors.

Berries, lemon, orange, floral flavors and mints don’t work well. They may in small amounts, but as a general rule I can’t recommend these pairings.
